Your house in Markham, and what we would do with it

Most of Markham is 1960s housing: ranches, raised ranches and split levels, masonry at the bottom and painted wood up top. Which puts most of the cost in reach and in preparation. Painting a Markham house is not a wall-area job, it is a trim and access job.

In Markham that mostly means exterior painting and interior painting, with cabinet refinishing on the same visit often enough that splitting them wastes everyone's time. We are 11.4 straight-line miles away at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview.

The short answers

  • Can we do your job? Almost certainly. In Markham it is exterior painting and interior painting most weeks, plus the drywall, plaster and carpentry that goes underneath both.
  • What will it cost? There is no price list on this site, because there is no honest local one to publish yet. Every job is quoted after we walk it. What moves the number on a Markham house is how much of the painted wood is up high, because reach costs more than wall area does.
  • What usually needs doing first? Usually the soffit, fascia and gable ends. They fail years before the brick underneath them needs anything.
  • When can you come? We are 11.4 straight-line miles out, and travel is not a hidden line on a quote from us. Ask before you plan around a date. Markham is out at the range where the size of the work and the week have to make sense together, and a straight no in advance beats a missed appointment.

The parts of a Markham quote that actually move

On a 1963 house the wall area outside is usually small and the detail is not. Fascia, soffit, the garage door surround, the front entry and the window trim is a narrow band of work that adds up, and it is exactly what gets underestimated by anyone quoting off photographs instead of standing there. 2,701 households own in Markham and 1,052 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

Old paint in Markham, and how it has to be handled

Paint from before 1978 can contain lead, and 1960s housing is the normal case in Markham. The practical effect is not that the work cannot be done. It is that it has to be contained and cleaned up to a standard, which is time at the start of a Markham job and time at the end of it.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in a Markham room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 2,701 homes worth of 1963-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Markham.

82.3 percent of housing units were built before 1980, the nearest bucket to the 1978 line that the Census publishes, and that is the reading for Markham. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

None of that is a reason to leave a Markham house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Questions

Asked about Markham

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Markham?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 82.3 percent of housing units in Markham went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.

Do you actually come out to Markham, or is this just a page?

It is 11.4 straight-line miles from the shop in Bridgeview, so it is a genuine drive and the answer depends on the job. A full exterior or a whole interior is worth the trip. One small patch on its own usually is not, and you will be told that rather than quoted a number that quietly covers the travel. Call 708-935-4289 and ask before you plan around it.

Is the $119,500 median home value in Markham what a job here costs?

No. That figure describes the houses, not the work. $119,500 is what the Census estimates a home in Markham is worth, and it earns its place on this page because value tracks size and age, which is what a painter is actually pricing. There is no price list on this site because there is no honest local one to publish yet.
